title: Concurrency-Aware Register Stacks for Efficient GPU Function Calls
problem: Function calls on GPUs incur significant runtime overhead through register spills/fills required to maintain function call ABI, placing substantial bandwidth and capacity pressure on shared GPU resources. This overhead limits practical use of functions for code organization and modularity in GPU kernels.
motivation: Function calls enable code reuse and maintainability, but their overhead on GPUs necessitates efficient hardware mechanisms to make them practical without sacrificing performance.
method: CARS repurposes segments of the GPU's register file (fast memory where computations store intermediate values) as software-controlled stacks for function calls. It exploits the fact that function prologues and epilogues (the setup and cleanup code at function boundaries) follow predictable patterns, enabling registers to be renamed using simple base-plus-offset addressing. The system analyzes the call graph (which functions call which others) and monitors runtime behavior to decide how many stacks to create, balancing stack capacity against the need for enough parallel computations to hide processing latencies.
key_novelty: The core idea is to dynamically allocate sections of the GPU's register file as stacks for function calls, sized to maintain high occupancy (keeping enough parallel computations running to hide processing delays).
contributions: Quantification of function call overhead impact on GPU bandwidth and register file pressure
CARS hardware mechanism that repurposes register file as efficient function call stack
Concurrency-aware resource allocation balancing stack space with GPU occupancy
26% performance improvement and 28% energy efficiency gain on function-calling applications
limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed in abstract; maintains compatibility with function-free programs.
primary_theme: efficient GPU function calls via concurrency-aware register stacking
